KP 3. Finding the Reduced Row Echelon Form of a Singular 3x3 System With Two Pivots
11.?

Consider the following system of linear equations: {−3x−3y+6z=9−x+4z=4x+y−2z=−3 Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix M of the system to reduced row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.

H
Thu, Oct 8th @ 1:48 AM|Elapsed: 0:16Incorrect

The augmented matrix for this system is M=[−3−369−104411−2−3].

Transforming M into reduced row echelon form, we have

M∼[−3−369−104411−2−3]R1↔R3∼[11−2−3−1044−3−369]R2:=R2+R1∼[11−2−30121−3−369]R3:=R3+3R1∼[11−2−301210000]

In the row echelon form above, we have only two pivots (in the 1st and 2nd columns). To transform the matrix to reduced row echelon form, we need to create zeros above the pivots only. This gives,

M∼[11−2−301210000]R1:=R1−R2∼[10−4−401210000].

The corresponding system is now {x−4z=−4y+2z=10=0.

Since any numbers x,y,z form a solution of the final equation, we can remove this equation from the system.

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variables are x and y, and we have one free variable, z. That means we need to find x and y in terms of z.

Therefore, the general solution is

{x=4z−4y=1−2zz=z,

where z (the free variable) is an arbitrary number.

In vector form, the solution can be written as [xyz]=[4z−41−2zz],z∈(−∞,∞).

Your Answer:
[4z+42z−1z],z∈(−∞,∞)
